title: Cross-SDK Retry Profiles, Idempotency-First Client Patterns, and Streaming Conflict Resolution
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and implement opinionated, easily consumable retry/backoff profiles across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs; design an idempotency-first client pattern for request keys; and establish ergonomic streaming conflict resolution behavior. This ticket captures the cross-language policy defaults, the taxonomy of retryable errors (including model-internal transient errors, infra/transient network errors, rate limit semantics, and determinism concerns), concrete example patterns for clients, and sample snippets illustrating how SDK consumers should use idempotency keys with streaming and non-streaming APIs.
acceptance_criteria: A short set of canonical retry profiles (fast-retry, balanced, conservative) defined and documented with numeric backoff parameters and jitter strategy
SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go) expose a consistent API to select a profile and override parameters at call time
Idempotency-first client helper that generates stable idempotency keys for common request types and documents when keys must be provided by callers
Clear retryable error taxonomy merged into SDK docs with mapping rules (retry, do-not-retry, conditional-retry-with-idempotency) and test coverage
Streaming endpoints can be resumed safely when server supports stream-resume tokens; otherwise clients fall back to idempotent restart semantics and surface clear guidance
Design doc and cross-team review comments addressed; at least one PR across SDKs with tests and integration job green
tasks: Draft design doc with profiles and taxonomy (this ticket)
Prototype Python helper: RetryProfile enum + IdempotencyKey util
Prototype TypeScript helper: profiles + streaming resume helpers
Prototype Go helper: lightweight profiles and recommended defaults
Add table-driven tests for mapping HTTP/gRPC errors to taxonomy
Update SDK docs and quickstart examples
Open cross-SDK PRs, address feedback, and merge
design_decisions: Expose only three named profiles to users by default to keep ergonomics simple (fast-retry, balanced, conservative); allow parameter overrides for advanced users
Default backoff: balanced uses exponential base=200ms, max=8s, multiplier=2.0, full jitter; fast-retry reduces max to 2s and multiplier to 1.6; conservative uses base=500ms and max=30s
Idempotency keys: SDK generates a deterministic key for idempotent operations based on (client_id, route, stable_payload_digest) but allows callers to supply explicit keys for business semantics
Streaming resume: prefer server-issued resume tokens when available; if not available, fall back to idempotent replay of the last N tokens where N=prefix_length (documented tradeoffs)
Rate limits: treat HTTP 429 with Retry-After header as retryable under balanced/conservative; fast-retry will surface to caller after 1-2 attempts unless caller supplies idempotency key
Do-not-retry: 4xx application-level errors (validation, auth) except 429 and 409 (conditional on idempotency)
error_taxonomy: infrastructure_transient: network timeouts, connection resets, socket errors => retryable
service_transient: internal server errors (5xx), model-internal timeouts => retryable with backoff
rate_limit: 429 with Retry-After => conditional retryable depending on profile and Retry-After value
conflict_non_idempotent: 409 on non-idempotent write => do-not-retry unless caller supplied idempotency key and semantics allow safe replay
undetermined_model_failure: model returned partial or malformed streaming frames => treat as service_transient for streaming resume when resume token available, else surface to caller
examples: TypeScript: const client = new Redwood({ retryProfile: 'fast' }); const key = idempotency.for({tenant,route,payloadHash}); await client.chat.stream({ messages, idempotencyKey: key })
Go: opts := sdk.DefaultOptions(); opts.RetryProfile = sdk.RetryProfileConservative; c := sdk.NewClient(opts); resp, err := c.Embed(ctx, req, sdk.WithIdempotency(key))

Streaming: when server returns resume_token in stream metadata, SDK will call stream.Resume(resume_token) transparently and emit consolidated events to user; when not available, SDK will re-request from last safe checkpoint and mark possible duplication
testing_plan: Table-driven unit tests mapping HTTP/gRPC status codes and underlying network errors to taxonomy
End-to-end flaky network simulation in CI job that toggles between fast/balanced/conservative profiles and asserts idempotent semantics for replayable requests
Streaming integration test that verifies resume token usage and correctness under partial-frame injection
Performance test to ensure retry overhead under balanced profile is within target SLO (p99 latency x retry attempts budget)
